sentences.text: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR

ORDER 18/08/2023 This application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner, in connection with FIR No.227/2021 registered at Police Station Kuchera, District Nagaur, for offences under Sections 420, 406, 465, 468, 120-B IPC, 66 and 66-D of Information Technology Act.
As per prosecution, complainant - Hari Ram received a message from Sandesh Company IRDA asking him to send his ID numbers so that his insurance can be done.

Believing upon the aforesaid statement, the complainant gave his ID number and transferred sums of Rs.1,67,454/- in RBS Account No.10065151892 (Account No.1), Rs.49,76,068/- in Geetajani Services Account No.10065151892 (Account No.2), Rs.49,76,068/- in Account of IDFC Mumbai, 90,78,280/- in Account No.201001789226 (Account No.3) of Rahul Kumar of (2 of 3) [CRLMB-4362/2023]
Indosan Mumbai and Rs.19,64,656/- in account No.50100473164768 (Account No.4) of Mohd.
Nadeem Waski of HDFC Bank through RTGS.
As per prosecution, the accused persons created fake messages for insurance scheme and IDs thereof and got huge amounts transferred in their personal accounts.

Co-accused Sahil Beri in his disclosure statement recorded under Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act informed that a part of the amount received by him has been transferred in favour of present petitioner.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case only the basis of the information given by the co-accused Sahil Beri.
Learned counsel submitted that apart from the disclosure statement of the co-accused, there is no other direct/corroboratory evidence showing involvement of the petitioner in the alleged crime.
Learned counsel further submitted that co-accused Sahil has categorically stated that the amount was transferred as per instructions of one Shri Sriram who is maternal uncle of the petitioner.
Learned counsel submitted that no recovery is due to be made from the petitioner and therefore, his custodial interrogation is not at all required.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application.
This Court directed learned Public Prosecutor to procure the case diary.
In compliance of the order passed by this Court, case diary has been produced for its perusal.
] From the perusal of the case diary, this Court finds that investigation has been kept pending against the present petitioner under Section 173(8) Cr.P.C.

Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not only required to determine the modus operandi but is also required for the recovery of amount allegedly transferred in the accounts of accused persons, a part whereof was given to the petitioner.

In view of aforesaid facts and also taking into consideration the nature and gravity of accusation so also the fact that a part of the amount transferred to co-accused Sahil was handed over to the present petitioner coupled with the argument of learned Public Prosecutor that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required to determine the modus operandi of the fraud, cannot be brushed aside.
Looking to the nature and seriousness of the accusation, this Court does not find any merit in the instant bail application which is dismissed as such.

(KULDEEP MATHUR)J /tarun goyal/ Sr.No.218 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
